title: Stop-loss approximation for normalized Rademacher sums
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every natural number $m$ and every real threshold $t$, the absolute difference between the expected positive part of a normalized sum of $m+1$ independent uniform signs minus $t$ and the standard Gaussian stop-loss value at $t$ is at most $C/\sqrt{m+1}$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a real constant $C$ with $C>0$
